status: author assessment of the cited results; not peer reviewed

results.label: lem:slip
results.title: Per-segment slip
results.assessment: GENERALIZES; pooled formula fails for persistent retries
results.conditions: Constant conditional acceptance a>0 and bad-acceptance b on reached attempts suffice for b/a. IID retries imply this.
results.failure_or_limit: A persistent easy/bad mixture gives bad emission 1/2, while first-attempt pooling predicts 1/3. Stalling is separate.

results.label: thm:threshold
results.title: Threshold and logarithmic overhead
results.assessment: PRESERVED under stronger conditional controls; constant arrival rate is unnecessary
results.conditions: Uniform p<=pbar<1, gate edge gamma>0, conditional gate independence and bounded attempt cost on every reachable history.
results.failure_or_limit: Average gate accuracy does not imply a conditional edge. Persistent bad states or vanishing progress can break cost and reliability bounds. The converse needs persistent conditional fault exposure.

results.label: thm:ceiling
results.title: Horizon ceiling
results.assessment: GENERALIZES to conditional exposure; a fixed marginal floor is insufficient
results.conditions: Immediate acceptance of first-attempt stealth faults, eventual emission, and lower bounds on p_i(h)*sigma_i(h) along correct prefixes.
results.failure_or_limit: Shared faults can give constant 0.99 survival at every horizon. The exact constant-Poisson multiplier can be strengthened using the acceptance denominator, not only the coarse p*sigma bound. The 1/sigma multiplier survives rate mixing with Z-independent visibility, is an upper bound under IFR, and can be exceeded under DFR.
results.p5_connection: prop:floor; cor:finitefloor; prop:mixing; prop:monotone; ex:shared; tests conditional_floor_and_finite_poisson_strengthening, shared_and_summable_counterexamples, rate_mixing_preserves_multiplier and monotone_hazard_orders_multiplier

results.label: cor:diversity
results.title: Diversity multiplies the ceiling
results.assessment: PRESERVED as a conditional event identity
results.conditions: Stealth events are independent under the operative distribution conditional on a bad candidate.
results.failure_or_limit: Different family names, independent development, or independent time steps do not establish this independence. Changing the fault distribution can remove it.

results.label: prop:decomp
results.title: Stealth decomposition
results.assessment: MIXTURE IDENTITY PRESERVED; horizon consequence needs exposure assumptions
results.conditions: The common stealth event has mass sigma_irr; outside it, family stealth events are independent with probability rho. Preserve the Poisson/fresh-retry model for its exact constant-rate horizon consequence; the source proof gives that form only to first order, and cor:finitefloor supplies it exactly under fresh retries (errata candidate 2).
results.failure_or_limit: The geometric breadth law fails without its conditional independence model. A local irreducible fraction alone does not imply a finite horizon when production exposure declines.

results.label: thm:interval
results.title: Optimal checkpoint interval
results.assessment: MODEL-SPECIFIC; replace for heterogeneous or persistent faults
results.conditions: The stated approximate cost model, fixed gate error/cost, constant lambda, and G*lambda small for the square-root approximation.
results.failure_or_limit: Mean-rate substitution underestimates expected cost when segment difficulty stays fixed across fresh retries, including for a deterministic lambda(t) by work position. The gap holds at every interval and at the optima, where it can be small (1.8530 vs 1.7951 in the example). eq:checkpoint applies only to an s-independent rate distribution; for a fixed profile the segment averages change with s. The printed minimum also drops the 1/(1-beta_m) factor (errata candidate 3). A different reset law changes the result. P1's limitations claim (mean unchanged, only variance) is an errata candidate.

results.label: thm:gg1
results.title: GG1: generated gates inherit the generator's stealth
results.assessment: PRESERVED without an arrival process
results.conditions: Fixed representation classes, decisions measurable in those classes, zero false rejection with the specified good-class support; the tolerance form also needs finite likelihood-ratio control.
results.failure_or_limit: A moving fault distribution changes the blind-set mass. Changed representation or semantics can change the set. This does not cover every machine-executed test authored by a model.

results.label: thm:gg2
results.title: GG2: the self-generation floor is a fixed point at $\lF$
results.assessment: LOWER BOUND PRESERVED for sound stacks; equality requires additional reachability
results.conditions: Every allowed gate preserves the stealth set; achieving equality also requires reachable coverage of all nonstealth fault mass.
results.failure_or_limit: A closure containing only accept-all gates has escape 1 even if stealth mass is smaller. Per-gate rejection tolerances do not automatically control an arbitrary conjunction. This qualification is independent of arrivals and partly flagged by the published README.
results.p5_connection: prop:blind; paper section on qualifications independent of fault arrivals

results.label: prop:exo
results.title: Exogenous family: independent stealth multiplies the floor
results.assessment: INTERSECTION PRESERVED; multiplication is conditional
results.conditions: Ideal stacks accept exactly their stealth sets on faulty candidates; product formula needs independence under the current fault measure.
results.failure_or_limit: Strict improvement needs positive removed mass, with set relations read modulo null sets as the source specifies. Nonideal stacks may pass extra nonstealth faults.

results.label: prop:ground
results.title: Reality-grounding: the non-representational escape
results.assessment: COVERED-SCOPE ZERO ESCAPE PRESERVED; residual equality needs qualification
results.conditions: The oracle decides the current correctness predicate on its covered scope.
results.failure_or_limit: An oracle arbitrary off scope can reject additional stealth there. A nonideal family stack can also leave extra nonstealth escapes. Exact residual requires an ideal family stack and off-scope oracle acceptance of the remaining stealth.

results.label: thm:escape
results.title: Series-system escape identity
results.assessment: GENERALIZES; independent product fails under arbitrary dependence
results.conditions: For unequal independent emitted-unit risks use 1-product(1-f_i). Its preceding accepted-output Bayes formula also needs the correct retry sampling law.
results.failure_or_limit: Replace marginals by correct-prefix conditional risks for dependent output sequences; a common fault can give all-correct probability 0.99 at every length.
results.p5_connection: prop:survival; prop:retry; ex:shared; tests chain_rule_and_marginal_bounds and persistent_retry_counterexample

results.label: cor:zero
results.title: Zero-escape needs a zero floor
results.assessment: PRESERVED under constant correct-prefix risk; replace for varying risks
results.conditions: Constant correct-prefix risk q_i=f suffices; independence across outputs is not needed (a geometric first-failure index gives dependent outputs with the same survival). Triangular arrays: the stated n*f_n scaling.
results.failure_or_limit: Positive risks at every step can be summable. Constant positive marginals with complete dependence need not imply escape tends to one. For a triangular array, vanishing escape is equivalent to vanishing sum of conditional risks.

results.label: prop:cost
results.title: Cost separation
results.assessment: PRESERVED without Poisson arrivals if per-unit cost laws remain
results.conditions: Power-law scaling above the floor, geometric reduction of conditional false acceptance, fixed prevalence and positive good-acceptance, and the stated cost assumptions.
results.failure_or_limit: A change in fault mix or gate dependence can remove geometric improvement. A changing good-acceptance rate can alter the escape transformation. Output-level targets require an appropriate dependence calculation.
results.p5_connection: sec:audit; eq:marginal; no new empirical support for the source cost-law hypothesis

results.label: lem:harris
results.title: Association product form; Esary--Proschan--Walkup
results.assessment: PRESERVED without constant intensity
results.conditions: Nonnegative bounded same-direction monotone functions of independent primitive variables.
results.failure_or_limit: Arbitrary history-dependent or negatively dependent models need not satisfy association.

results.label: prop:corr
results.title: Correlated-escape bound
results.assessment: PRESERVED under monotone provenance; not a general dependence bound
results.conditions: The source independent-primitive monotone model and fixed marginals; strictness additionally uses joint pivotality and nondegenerate survival factors.
results.failure_or_limit: Disjoint risk-0.1 events give union 0.2, above the independent product value 0.19. Clustering at fixed marginals does not establish lower damage or deployment benefit.

results.label: prop:ra
results.title: R-A: horizon under partial closure
results.assessment: GENERALIZES; stationary mixed ceiling fails without its assumptions
results.conditions: Independent stationary routing/input vectors, fixed mechanisms and semantics, open-path floor, and the stated fallback interpretation.
results.failure_or_limit: Shared/repeated inputs can exceed the product upper bound. Different work regions have different exposure, so equal work share need not remove equal risk. Build-mean risk cannot be plugged into a conditional upper bound.
results.p5_connection: prop:closure; ex:shared; errata candidate 2 (closed-branch (1+O(lambda s)) factor is necessary); tests routing_and_feedback_counterexample, shared_and_summable_counterexamples and closed_path_exceeds_first_order_horizon

results.label: prop:twin
results.title: Evidence does not separate twins
results.assessment: PRESERVED; IID sampling can be weakened
results.conditions: Equal joint observation-record and auxiliary-randomness laws, a fixed target fault functional, and validity over the same mechanism class.
results.failure_or_limit: Mechanism-identity side channels or nonshared sample laws can distinguish twins. The result constrains evidence, not the actual mechanism fault rate.

results.label: cor:samefamily
results.title: Same-family evidence
results.assessment: PRESERVED under the representation and mechanism-class assumptions
results.conditions: Evidence is constant on family classes. Explicit twin-mass equality also needs the countable scope and finite-patch closure.
results.failure_or_limit: A different target distribution changes twin mass; unrestricted text review is outside the pointwise evidence model. Evidence that is not decided within F (e.g. exact correctness evidence) can separate F-twins and remove the conclusion. Authorship alone does not establish deciding-substrate restriction.

results.label: prop:replay
results.title: Exact replay transfers the fault mass of the reference
results.assessment: PRESERVED pointwise under every fixed target distribution
results.conditions: Reference defined on the entire claimed scope; error and disagreement measured under the same target law.
results.failure_or_limit: A recorded scope may not cover deployment. Drift can change both error and disagreement; old masses cannot be reused without control.
results.p5_connection: prop:drift; exhaustive replay check in twins_replay_and_repair

results.label: cor:replayfloor
results.title: A copy of accepted outputs inherits the floor
results.assessment: PRESERVED without fresh retries; only the proof's intermediate denominator step needs them
results.conditions: Every input eventually emits; first-attempt raw p_x and fault law; same-family sound acceptance of stealth; retained acceptance sound or empty; disagreement subtraction.
results.failure_or_limit: The displayed bound p*lambda_F - E[delta] follows from first-attempt stealth passing immediately under eventual emission; fresh retries only give the intermediate improvement p_x*mu_x/A_x. Changing within-family visibility (e.g. an exact reference gate) removes the floor. Selection by discarding builds or a new input law requires reanalysis. This is an expectation over references, not every deployed build.

results.label: prop:produced
results.title: Produced faults that nothing detects
results.assessment: PRESERVED independently of arrival stationarity
results.conditions: Input independent of build under the stated target law, every build deployed, repair preserves all outputs in the undetected set; family specialization also needs representation/support/tolerance assumptions.
results.failure_or_limit: Broad repairs can fix undetected faults; selective rejection of builds changes the deployed population. Both parts depend on visibility: the first through the undetected set U, the second (family specialization, lambda_F^B - kappa*rho_0) through within-family indistinguishability; detecting previously invisible build faults removes the floor. The generalizing-builder hypothesis remains untested.
results.p5_connection: prop:blind; prop:drift; preservation control in twins_replay_and_repair

results.label: prop:rc
results.title: R-C: break-even with the validation cost
results.assessment: ACCOUNTING GENERALIZES; sample and separability claims retain separate assumptions
results.conditions: Use actual expected per-call costs, build/validation/upkeep costs and lifetime. Original sample necessity assumes independent exact target validation and candidate masses approaching theta; frontier selection assumes additive uncoupled regions.
results.failure_or_limit: Repeated validation inputs do not buy the stated confidence. Conditional exposure gives only a sufficient sample count; the source's necessary count needs its independent target sampling and near-threshold class, and targeted validation can need far fewer items. Random lifetime/demand correlations and shared maintenance costs preclude products of means or independent region choices.

results.label: prop:rd
results.title: R-D: composition of the residual part
results.assessment: PRESERVED under completeness and monotone provenance
results.conditions: All residual failure modes covered; fixed finite tree with acceptance descending to children; escape indicators monotone in independent primitives.
results.failure_or_limit: Without association retain only the union bound. Without residual completeness an interaction can make a parent wrong while all named child/projection indicators are zero.

results.label: cor:reach
results.title: Reach and residual
results.assessment: PRESERVED under constant correct-prefix risk q(c); replace under feedback or selected closure
results.conditions: Correct-prefix risk q_i(c)=q(c) with fixed branch parameters as c varies; independence across outputs is not needed. Fault-free rejection-free closure for the stated ideal gain.
results.failure_or_limit: Closing easy work can remove little risk. A locally safer step can alter future state and reduce total survival. Fallback can retain finite risk even with a correct mechanism.

results.label: prop:load
results.title: R-E: bounded load
results.assessment: ALREADY NONCONSTANT; preserved under its stated intensity bounds
results.conditions: Poisson arrivals with deterministic load path, load-monotone hazard, specified positive bounds and executor/open-work clock. Uniform conditional first-fault bounds can support related survival comparisons but are an additional assumption.
results.failure_or_limit: Bounded context alone proves neither hazard monotonicity nor a clean reset. A random environment's mean intensity cannot replace conditional hazard. The load and closure gains have different baselines.
results.p5_connection: sec:hazard; ex:latent; prop:monotone (nondecreasing load makes the ungated agent IFR; if it is also gated under the cor:finitefloor model, 1/sigma bounds the gated multiplier up to rounding); tests latent_rate_and_mean_cost and monotone_hazard_orders_multiplier
